title: 手書き注文 集計アシスタント
brief: Build a mobile-first installable PWA for a client workflow currently done on paper. Primary v1 goal: capture/upload one or more handwritten Japanese order sheets, extract product names and quantities, merge equivalent products, and output a clean total picking list. The app must have an adaptive local database: canonical products have stable IDs; aliases/handwriting/OCR variants are linked to canonical products; when a user manually maps an unknown/ambiguous reading to a product, store that correction so future matching improves. Store optional location labels A/B/C/D/E and location history per product; unknown locations remain unassigned and can be assigned later. Include confidence states and a review queue rather than silently guessing. Architecture must be provider-agnostic: define an AI adapter interface with Manual/ChatGPT handoff mode and API-ready adapters, but DO NOT commit or expose any API key. For this prototype, provide a fully functional offline/demo analysis path using editable pasted structured JSON/sample data so UI/database/picking workflow can be tested immediately without secrets. Persist client-side data in IndexedDB/localStorage with export/import JSON so the whole learned database can later be migrated to the client's environment. Include product master, aliases, recognition history, location history, sessions, settings, and backup/restore. UI should be very simple: Home -> Take/select photo -> Analyze/review -> totals grouped by location -> print/share. Add a data-management screen for products/aliases/locations and a correction workflow that offers candidate matches. Japanese UI. No external runtime dependency on VoiceDev Master. Avoid secrets and personal data. Include README/handoff notes for future secure backend/API integration and client migration.
